archetype.name: Point Guard (short-area distributor)
archetype.definition: Nix wins by getting the ball out short and spreading it among five regular targets while rarely taking a sack, and he takes only an occasional shot downfield rather than living outside the numbers.

report.headline: A winning short-game distributor whose efficiency finally caught up to the record
report.take:
Nix in year three is a game-running passer more than a game-breaking one. The Broncos are 7-2 and have won five straight, but his full-season efficiency is ordinary: 0.014 EPA per dropback ranks 26th of 49, 6.03 yards per attempt ranks 38th, and his volume has slipped from 231.2 passing yards a game last year to 192.2. That fits his career. His YPA has gone 6.66, 6.42, now 6.03, and he has never ranked better than 23rd in EPA per play. What has always held up is the floor. He doesn't take sacks: his 3.7% sack rate is seventh, his pressure-to-sack rate of 18.5% is sixth, and his offense allows hits at the second-lowest rate in the league. He also doesn't throw many picks, with a 1.4% interception rate against a 2.4% league average.

The passing game splits cleanly by depth. On throws of 0-9 air yards he is very good: 0.189 EPA, a 68.8% completion rate and 4.5 points of CPOE on 141 attempts. That is his real skill. Two things drag it down. The first is the screen and swing game, 78 throws behind the line that cost 16.3 EPA. The second is the intermediate window, where he completes 41.5% at 10.7 points under expected and has thrown three of his four interceptions. The deep ball has worked on a small sample (0.311 EPA on 27 attempts), but he rarely goes there, and his throws land 2.48 yards short of the sticks on average.

Third down is the season's biggest hidden problem. He faces an average of 7.7 yards to go, converts 26.7% of the time, and those plays have cost 33.1 EPA. That is the clearest sign of an offense that wins early downs and then can't finish drives through the air. The record also hides how much has come from the defense and from close-game play. He has been sharp in one-score fourth quarters (0.229 EPA) and poor once the Broncos lead by two scores (-0.391), which partly reflects Sean Payton shutting the offense down with a lead.

The good news is that the last three weeks look like a different passer. Since Week 7 he is at 0.19 EPA per dropback and 7.45 adjusted net yards per dropback, with CPOE back to plus-0.9. Pat Bryant's emergence has helped: 0.99 EPA per target on 18 looks. The stretch came against two soft defenses and Kansas City, though, so it is an upgrade to watch rather than a new baseline.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance and ball security
strengths.body: He gets rid of the ball, and the line keeps him clean. His sack rate is among the league's lowest, and pressure rarely turns into a sack. This has been true in all three seasons, with pressure-to-sack ranks of 10th, 7th and now 6th, so it is who he is and not luck. It keeps drives alive and gives his stat lines a floor.

strengths.title: Accurate, efficient short passing
strengths.body: Throws of 0-9 air yards are the engine of this offense. He completes them well above expectation and creates positive plays nearly half the time. It is the bulk of his attempts and it is stable, because it rests on timing and accuracy rather than big plays.

strengths.title: Recent surge in efficiency
strengths.body: Over the last three games his EPA per dropback has jumped well above his season mark, with better accuracy and more touchdowns. Bryant's big plays and a healthier deep game explain much of it. Two of the three opponents were bottom-tier defenses, so treat it as real but inflated.

concerns.title: Third downs are a drive-killer
concerns.body: On third down he converts barely a quarter of the time and has lost a large chunk of EPA. Long yardage plays a part, but so do the throws he's asked to make. His weakest zone is 10-19 yards, and that is exactly where third-and-long is won. This is more a real limitation than noise: it lines up with his intermediate accuracy.

concerns.title: Screen game is burning plays
concerns.body: The 78 throws behind the line of scrimmage have cost more EPA than any other depth and come in well below expected completion. That is partly scheme, since Payton leans on screens as an extension of the run game. Still, it is a big share of his attempts producing negative value, and it drags his yards per attempt down.

concerns.title: Legs and fumbles both slipping
concerns.body: His rushing is down from last year. Designed runs are getting stuffed and gain under two yards a carry, so the dual-threat element that boosted his rookie line has faded outside one 73-yard game at Arizona. He has also lost two fumbles and has eight turnover-worthy fumbles. That rate is more about ball security than bad luck.

trend.note: Weeks 5 and 6 were the low point, at 123 and 107 passing yards. Since then he has posted positive passing EPA in three straight games, with 0.19 EPA per dropback in that stretch, and the team hasn't lost since Week 4.

nextGame.headline: Worst short-pass defense in the league meets his best zone
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas is close to the ideal opponent for how Nix plays. The Raiders rank 28th in defensive EPA and 28th against the pass. They are dead last in EPA allowed on short throws, the 0-9 yard window where Nix does most of his good work. Their success rate allowed ranks 31st, which suits an offense that wants to move the chains rather than hit home runs. They have given quarterbacks the most touchdowns per game in the league, and the opposing WR2 role has feasted against them. The Book hasn't posted a line yet, and there is no forecast of note.

Availability matters most on his side. Jaylen Waddle, his top target by volume and his most efficient high-volume wideout, left the Carolina game with a concussion. He is questionable, with an expected return date of the game itself, so the bye week is his best chance to clear protocol. Without him, more targets go to Courtland Sutton, who has been negative per target, and to Bryant, which raises the variance. On the Raiders' side, rotational DT Thomas Booker IV is out, a small hit to an interior rush that is already middling.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs. a broken underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: Nix's best throws are the quick, short ones, and Las Vegas allows more EPA on short passes than any defense in the league. That should let him string together completions and stay ahead of the third-and-long situations that have been his weakness.

keyMatchups.title: Sutton in the WR2 spot
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders have let the opposing WR2 score far above his usual output, the worst mark in the league. Sutton has been Nix's least efficient target, so this is the spot where that could turn around, especially if Waddle plays and Sutton stays in the WR2 role.

keyMatchups.title: Waddle's concussion status
keyMatchups.body: Waddle leads the team in targets and is positive per target. If he sits, the passing game leans on Bryant's big plays and Engram, and Las Vegas sends tight ends an above-average share of targets. His status will decide whether Nix gets a spread-it-around day or a narrower one.

nextGame.watch: Watch his third-down conversion rate. Against this defense, if he can't stay on schedule, the recent surge is mostly about the opponents he has faced.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the floor to hold and the ceiling to stay modest. The sack avoidance, low interception rate and short-area accuracy have held up for three seasons, and they will keep producing efficient, mid-volume games, roughly 200-245 passing yards with a touchdown or two. The last three weeks are likely somewhere between his true level and his season line. The schedule softened, Bryant's per-target EPA won't stay near 1.0, and the deep-ball success came on only 27 attempts. Even so, 0.19 EPA per dropback isn't a baseline to bank on.

What would really change his outlook is the middle of the field. If the intermediate accuracy recovers toward his career norms, the third-down problem shrinks and his yards per attempt climbs back toward last year's level. If it doesn't, he stays a mid-pack efficiency passer on a team that wins through defense and close games. The rushing should bounce back some from this year's low, but the designed runs aren't working, and the 73-yard Arizona game looks like the exception rather than the rule.

confidence.note: Nine starts and a three-season career make the traits clear, but the recent surge rests on three games, two against weak defenses, and Waddle's status is uncertain.
